summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held posts as an assistant professor at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996-2003).

Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist. He earned a BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1992-1996) and a doctorate at Leiden University (1997-2005), studying under Alexander Lubotsky and Saul Migron.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania (1996) under Victor H. Mair, later serving as an associate professor at Cornell University.

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale (B.A. 1963) and Harvard (Master's 1965, 1972), and took a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Humboldt University. He served as librarian at Yale (1856-1872), president of the University of California (1872-1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins (1875-1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902-1904).

Daniel Cozort works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught as an assistant professor of religion at Dickinson College (~1988-2021).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a director of research at both the CNRS and Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

Daniel Franz Schauffelberger was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen, the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Bonn, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1845.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard University (A.B. ~1932-1936, A.M. ~1936-1938) and under Walter Eugene Clark and Kalipada Tarkacharya, later serving as an assistant professor at Harvard (1938-1983).

Daniel John Gogerly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818-1834), served as General Superintendent of the Wesleyan Mission in South Ceylon (1838), and held leadership roles at the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845-1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a master's at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973-2001).

Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1974. He held faculty posts at Dartmouth College (1971-1980), the University of Washington (1980-1995), and UCLA (1995-2018).

Daniel M. Stuart is a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who earned a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (attested 2012). He held an assistant professorship at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and a guest professorship at Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard University around 1978.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his thesis at Florida State University under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was a scholar of archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Strasbourg and Paris (Ph.D. 1950) under Henri Seyrig, later serving as inspector for the French antiquities service in the Levant (1929-1940) and professor at Strasbourg (1955).
Daniel Sperber is a historian and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1963-1968). He held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Virginia and University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2000). He served as professor at the University of Southern Mississippi (2000-2022) and adjunct professor at MSU Denver (2023).

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Tasmania, having studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.
